Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 2a) demonstrates marked asymmetry with a smaller, hyperlucent right hemithorax and diminished right pulmonary vascular markings compared to the left, which is characteristic of chronic right pulmonary artery obstruction or hypoplasia seen in Takayasu arteritis. The CT image (Figure 2b) confirms vascular pathology (arrow pointing to calcified/stenotic vessel), supporting a chronic vasculitic etiology rather than an acute embolic event or bilateral disease.
